response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.fundflux AS src, AVG(s.boxy / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS sz FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), a AS (SELECT AVG(sz) AS avg_sz FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_ratios, SUM(g.sz) AS combined_size, AVG(g.sz - a.avg_sz) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.sz > a.avg_sz

assumptions.assumption: A funding source's 'size' is the number of scanspatial rows linked to it through an inner join to projects. A NULL fundflux forms its own group, and GROUP BY keeps NULL as one group.
The average size is the unweighted mean of the per-source sizes. Only sources with size strictly above it are kept.
A boxz of 0 is treated as missing, via NULLIF, to avoid division by zero. Rows where boxy or boxz is NULL are ignored by AVG.
The result row's ratio is the plain average of the per-source average ratios. It is not weighted by size.

alternatives.interpretation: Size is the number of distinct projects per funding source that have spatial scans, not the number of spatial rows.
alternatives.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.fundflux AS src, AVG(s.boxy / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) AS sz FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), a AS (SELECT AVG(sz) AS avg_sz FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_ratios, SUM(g.sz) AS combined_size, AVG(g.sz - a.avg_sz) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.sz > a.avg_sz
